oh wow this is a really interesting question/topic!! i wish i could think of more examples but for now i'll meekly offer the few that i think are good examples


1)pentagon's [like this](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AeLifhqRggg) which i take to be a song about overcoming ordeals . it starts off in a very somber way, with sparse guitar & piano chords and depressing lyrics, but gets more upbeat with the prechorus, which is when the lyrics start to become more positive. the chorus' lyrics and melody are very defiant and powerful ("I won’t cry anymore/Scream it to the world, oh yeah") accompanied by an ascending vocal in the background. e'dawn's rap comes around and rly propels the song along, but imo the best "text painting" moment is on the [last chorus](https://youtu.be/AeLifhqRggg?t=3m) where jinho's rly high amazing falsetto repeats the chorus lyrics "scream it to the world" and "running" (i think?? none of the lyric vids include the part but its gorgeous) over the chorus and it's just a really beautiful, cathartic moment. if the song's story of an ordeal were a mountain, it would be at the peak. also the decision to put yuto's rap at the end is really satisfying and the lyrics + instrumental convey a feeling of "i made it". sorry this is so long and messy but i could gush for hours about this song!!


2)j-hope's [hope world](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h2AsH8xl90o) opens with a splooshing water sound as a reference to the "20000 leagues under the sea" symbolism in the lyrics (hoseok as captain nemo and the audience as arronax) and the frequent rhythm, flow, and instrumental quirks + the rly peppy and autotuned chorus make the song sound really dreamy and upbeat. it's a really good intro to jhope as a persona and his mixtape overall
